## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lme4) # For mixed-effects modeling
library(readr)

```

```{r}
# Import the dataset
file_name <- "ADAP_Macula_GCC_dataset.csv"
data <- read_csv(file_name)

# Check the structure of the dataset
str(data)

# Summarize the dataset
summary(data)

# Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
# 1. Distribution of GCC thickness
ggplot(data, aes(x = GCC)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of GCC Thickness", x = "GCC Thickness (microns)", y = "Frequency")

# 2. GCC thickness over time
agg_data <- data %>%
  group_by(time) %>%
  summarize(mean_GCC = mean(GCC, na.rm = TRUE), sd_GCC = sd(GCC, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot(agg_data, aes(x = time, y = mean_GCC)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean_GCC - sd_GCC, ymax = mean_GCC + sd_GCC), alpha = 0.2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Mean GCC Thickness Over Time", x = "Time (years)", y = "Mean GCC Thickness (microns)")

# 3. Individual GCC trends
ggplot(data, aes(x = time, y = GCC, group = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Individual GCC Thickness Trends", x = "Time (years)", y = "GCC Thickness (microns)")

# Check for missing values
colSums(is.na(data))

# Basic statistics on GCC loss
# Calculate rate of change in GCC for each individual
data <- data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(time) %>%
  mutate(GCC_change = GCC - lag(GCC),
         Rate_of_Change = GCC_change / (time - lag(time)))

# Summary of GCC rate of change
data %>%
  summarise(mean_rate = mean(Rate_of_Change, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_rate = sd(Rate_of_Change, na.rm = TRUE),
            min_rate = min(Rate_of_Change, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_rate = max(Rate_of_Change, na.rm = TRUE))

```

```{r}
# Load necessary library
library(lme4)

# Fit a linear mixed-effects model
# Fixed effect: time
# Random effect: intercept for each individual (id)
time_trend_model <- lmer(GCC ~ time + (1 | id), data = data)

# Summary of the model
summary(time_trend_model)

# Visualize the population time trend
predicted_data <- data %>%
  group_by(time) %>%
  summarize(mean_predicted_GCC = predict(time_trend_model, newdata = data.frame(time = unique(time)), re.form = NA))

ggplot(data, aes(x = time, y = GCC)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, color = "gray") +
  geom_line(data = predicted_data, aes(x = time, y = mean_predicted_GCC), color = "blue", size = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 2: Population Time Trend for GCC Thickness",
    x = "Time (years)",
    y = "Predicted GCC Thickness (microns)"
  )

```

```{r}
# Load the necessary library
library(nlme)

# Fit models with different covariance structures
models <- list()

# 1. Random Intercept Only (RI)
models$RI <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, data = data, method = "REML")

# 2. Random Intercept and Slope (RIAS)
models$RIAS <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ time | id, data = data, method = "REML")

# 3. Compound Symmetry (CS)
models$CS <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corCompSymm(form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# 4. Autoregressive of order 1 (AR(1))
models$AR1 <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corAR1(form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# 5. Unstructured (UN)
models$UN <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corSymm(form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# 6. ARMA(1,1)
models$ARMA11 <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corARMA(p = 1, q = 1, form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# 7. ARMA(2,1)
models$ARMA21 <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corARMA(p = 2, q = 1, form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# 8. ARMA(2,0)
models$ARMA20 <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corARMA(p = 2, q = 0, form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# Compare models using AIC
model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = names(models),
  AIC = sapply(models, AIC)
)

# Sort models by AIC (lower is better)
model_comparison <- model_comparison[order(model_comparison$AIC), ]

# Print the comparison table
print(model_comparison)

```

```{r}
# Load the necessary library
library(nlme)
library(dplyr)

# Transform `time` into consecutive integers for each individual
data <- data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(time_int = rank(time)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Fit models with different covariance structures
models <- list()

# 1. Random Intercept Only (RI)
models$RI <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, data = data, method = "REML")

# 2. Random Intercept and Slope (RIAS)
models$RIAS <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ time | id, data = data, method = "REML")

# 3. Compound Symmetry (CS)
models$CS <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corCompSymm(form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# 4. Autoregressive of order 1 (AR(1))
models$AR1 <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corAR1(form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")


# 6. ARMA(1,1)
models$ARMA11 <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corARMA(p = 1, q = 1, form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# 7. ARMA(2,1)
models$ARMA21 <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corARMA(p = 2, q = 1, form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# 8. ARMA(2,0)
models$ARMA20 <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corARMA(p = 2, q = 0, form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# Compare models using AIC
model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = names(models),
  AIC = sapply(models, AIC)
)

# Sort models by AIC (lower is better)
model_comparison <- model_comparison[order(model_comparison$AIC), ]

# Print the comparison table
print(model_comparison)
```

```{r}
# Extract fixed effects (population average) from the RIAS model
fixed_effects <- fixef(models$RIAS)
population_rate_of_change <- fixed_effects["time"]

# Extract random effects (individual variability) from the RIAS model
random_effects <- ranef(models$RIAS)

# Calculate the range of individual slopes (rate of change)
individual_slopes <- random_effects$id$time + population_rate_of_change
slope_summary <- summary(individual_slopes)

# Print the results
cat("Population Average Rate of GCC Loss:\n")
cat(sprintf(" %.3f microns per year\n", population_rate_of_change))

cat("\nIndividual Variability in Rate of GCC Loss:\n")
cat(sprintf(" Range: %.3f to %.3f microns per year\n", min(individual_slopes), max(individual_slopes)))
cat(sprintf(" Mean: %.3f microns per year\n", mean(individual_slopes)))
cat(sprintf(" SD: %.3f microns per year\n", sd(individual_slopes)))

# Optional: Plot the distribution of individual rates of change
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data.frame(Slope = individual_slopes), aes(x = Slope)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Individual Rates of GCC Loss",
    x = "Rate of GCC Loss (microns/year)",
    y = "Frequency"
  )

```

```{r}
# Load the necessary library
library(nlme)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Transform `time` into consecutive integers for each individual
data <- data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(time_int = rank(time)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Fit Random Intercept and Slope (RIAS) model
RIAS_model <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ time | id, data = data, method = "REML")

# Extract fixed effects (population average)
population_rate_of_change <- fixef(RIAS_model)["time"]

# Extract random effects (individual variability)
random_effects <- ranef(RIAS_model)

# Calculate individual slopes (rate of GCC loss for each patient)
if ("time" %in% colnames(random_effects$id)) {
  individual_slopes <- random_effects$id$time + population_rate_of_change

  # Summary statistics for individual slopes
  slope_summary <- summary(individual_slopes)
  cat("Population Average Rate of GCC Loss:\n")
  cat(sprintf(" %.3f microns per year\n", population_rate_of_change))

  cat("\nIndividual Variability in Rate of GCC Loss:\n")
  cat(sprintf(" Range: %.3f to %.3f microns per year\n", min(individual_slopes), max(individual_slopes)))
  cat(sprintf(" Mean: %.3f microns per year\n", mean(individual_slopes)))
  cat(sprintf(" SD: %.3f microns per year\n", sd(individual_slopes)))

  # Plot the distribution of individual slopes
  ggplot(data.frame(Slope = individual_slopes), aes(x = Slope)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = "Distribution of Individual Rates of GCC Loss",
      x = "Rate of GCC Loss (microns/year)",
      y = "Frequency"
    )
} else {
  cat("Random slope for 'time' not found in the random effects!\n")
}

```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(nlme)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Prepare the data: ensure time is properly scaled and unique per individual
data <- data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(time_scaled = time - min(time)) %>% # Scale time to start from 0 for each individual
  ungroup()

# Fit Random Intercept and Slope (RIAS) model with proper random slope specification
RIAS_model <- lme(
  fixed = GCC ~ time, 
  random = ~ time | id, # Specify random intercept and slope for 'time'
  data = data, 
  method = "REML",
  control = lmeControl(msMaxIter = 100, opt = "optim") # Increase iteration limit for better convergence
)

# Extract fixed effects (population average rate of change)
population_rate_of_change <- fixef(RIAS_model)["time"]

# Extract random effects for individual slopes
random_effects <- ranef(RIAS_model)

# Check and calculate individual slopes
if ("time" %in% colnames(random_effects$id)) {
  # Combine population fixed effect and individual random slopes
  individual_slopes <- random_effects$id$time + population_rate_of_change
  
  # Summary statistics for individual slopes
  cat("Population Average Rate of GCC Loss:\n")
  cat(sprintf(" %.3f microns per year\n", population_rate_of_change))
  
  cat("\nIndividual Variability in Rate of GCC Loss:\n")
  cat(sprintf(" Range: %.3f to %.3f microns per year\n", min(individual_slopes), max(individual_slopes)))
  cat(sprintf(" Mean: %.3f microns per year\n", mean(individual_slopes)))
  cat(sprintf(" SD: %.3f microns per year\n", sd(individual_slopes)))
  
  # Plot the distribution of individual slopes
  ggplot(data.frame(Slope = individual_slopes), aes(x = Slope)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = "Distribution of Individual Rates of GCC Loss",
      x = "Rate of GCC Loss (microns/year)",
      y = "Frequency"
    )
} else {
  cat("Random slope for 'time' not found in the random effects! Re-check model specification.\n")
}

```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Calculate population average rate of GCC loss using linear regression
population_model <- lm(GCC ~ time, data = data)

# Extract the fixed effect for time (slope)
population_rate_of_change <- coef(population_model)["time"]

# Estimate individual slopes using linear regression for each patient
data_individual_slopes <- data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarize(
    individual_slope = coef(lm(GCC ~ time))["time"], # Slope for each individual
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Summarize individual slopes
slope_summary <- data_individual_slopes %>%
  summarize(
    min_slope = min(individual_slope),
    max_slope = max(individual_slope),
    mean_slope = mean(individual_slope),
    sd_slope = sd(individual_slope)
  )

# Print results
cat("Population Average Rate of GCC Loss:\n")
cat(sprintf(" %.3f microns per year\n", population_rate_of_change))

cat("\nIndividual Variability in Rate of GCC Loss:\n")
cat(sprintf(" Range: %.3f to %.3f microns per year\n", slope_summary$min_slope, slope_summary$max_slope))
cat(sprintf(" Mean: %.3f microns per year\n", slope_summary$mean_slope))
cat(sprintf(" SD: %.3f microns per year\n", slope_summary$sd_slope))

# Plot distribution of individual slopes
ggplot(data_individual_slopes, aes(x = individual_slope)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 4: Distribution of Individual Rates of GCC Loss",
    x = "Rate of GCC Loss (microns/year)",
    y = "Frequency"
  )

```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Investigate the relationship between initial GCC thickness and rate of GCC loss
# Calculate individual slopes for each patient
individual_slopes <- data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarize(
    initial_GCC = first(GCC), # Initial GCC thickness
    individual_slope = coef(lm(GCC ~ time))["time"], # Rate of GCC loss
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Fit a linear model to examine the relationship between initial GCC and rate of GCC loss
relationship_model <- lm(individual_slope ~ initial_GCC, data = individual_slopes)

# Summary of the relationship model
relationship_summary <- summary(relationship_model)
print(relationship_summary)

# Visualize the relationship between initial GCC and rate of GCC loss
ggplot(individual_slopes, aes(x = initial_GCC, y = individual_slope)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "blue") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 5: Relationship Between Initial GCC and Rate of GCC Loss",
    x = "Initial GCC Thickness (microns)",
    y = "Rate of GCC Loss (microns/year)"
  )

```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(nlme)
library(ggplot2)

# Base Model: Population intercept and slope only
base_model <- lme(
  fixed = GCC ~ time, 
  random = ~ time | id,  # Random intercept and slope
  data = data,
  method = "REML"
)

# Include Age: Age-adjusted model
age_model <- lme(
  fixed = GCC ~ time + base_age,  # Add age as a fixed effect
  random = ~ time | id,      # Random intercept and slope
  data = data,
  method = "REML"
)

# Summarize and compare models
base_summary <- summary(base_model)
age_summary <- summary(age_model)

# Print model summaries
cat("Base Model (No Age):\n")
print(base_summary)

cat("\nAge-Adjusted Model:\n")
print(age_summary)

# Extract fixed effects for interpretation
fixed_effects_age <- fixef(age_model)
cat("\nFixed Effects in Age-Adjusted Model:\n")
print(fixed_effects_age)

# Visualize the effects of age on GCC trends
ggplot(data, aes(x = time, y = GCC, color = bage)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", aes(group = id), se = FALSE, color = "blue", size = 0.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Effect of Age on GCC Trends",
    x = "Time (years)",
    y = "GCC Thickness (microns)",
    color = "Age"
  )

```

# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)

# Create GCC group based on median
data <- data %>%
  mutate(GCC_group = ifelse(GCC >= median(GCC, na.rm = TRUE), "High GCC", "Low GCC"))

# Summary statistics

  group_by(GCC_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    `GCC (Mean ± SD)` = paste0(
      round(mean(GCC, na.rm = TRUE), 2), " ± ", round(sd(GCC, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
    ),
    `Base Age (Mean ± SD)` = paste0(
      round(mean(base_age, na.rm = TRUE), 2), " ± ", round(sd(base_age, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
    ),
    `Time Range` = paste0("[", min(time, na.rm = TRUE), " - ", max(time, na.rm = TRUE), "]")
  )

# Add p-values
t_test_gcc <- t.test(GCC ~ GCC_group, data = data)
t_test_age <- t.test(base_age ~ GCC_group, data = data)

gcc_summary <- gcc_summary %>%
  mutate(
    `GCC p-value` = ifelse(GCC_group == "High GCC", round(t_test_gcc$p.value, 3), ""),
    `Base Age p-value` = ifelse(GCC_group == "High GCC", round(t_test_age$p.value, 3), "")
  )

# Create the table with gt
table_1 <- gt(gcc_summary) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Characteristics of GCC Groups",
    subtitle = "Comparing High GCC and Low GCC Groups"
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    GCC_group = "Group",
    n = "n",
    `GCC (Mean ± SD)` = "GCC (Mean ± SD)",
    `Base Age (Mean ± SD)` = "Base Age (Mean ± SD)",
    `Time Range` = "Time Range",
    `GCC p-value` = "GCC p-value",
    `Base Age p-value` = "Base Age p-value"
  ) %>%
  fmt_missing(columns = everything(), missing_text = "") %>%
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "p-values come from t-tests for quantitative measures.",
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = c(`GCC p-value`, `Base Age p-value`))
  ) %>%
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = "Table 1"
  )

# Display the table
table_1

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(nlme)
library(tidyverse)

# Prepare the dataset
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    time_squared = time^2,   # Quadratic term
    time_cubic = time^3      # Cubic term
  )

# Fit multiple models
# Linear model
model_linear <- lme(GCC ~ time, random = ~time | id, data = data, method = "REML")

# Quadratic model
model_quadratic <- lme(GCC ~ time + time_squared, random = ~time | id, data = data, method = "REML")

# Cubic model
model_cubic <- lme(GCC ~ time + time_squared + time_cubic, random = ~time | id, data = data, method = "REML")

# Compare models using AIC
aic_values <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Linear", "Quadratic", "Cubic"),
  AIC = c(AIC(model_linear), AIC(model_quadratic), AIC(model_cubic))
)
print(aic_values)

# Determine the best model
best_model <- aic_values[which.min(aic_values$AIC), ]
cat("Best model:", best_model$Model, "with AIC =", best_model$AIC, "\n")

# Add fitted values from the best model to the dataset
data$fitted <- ifelse(
  best_model$Model == "Linear", predict(model_linear),
  ifelse(best_model$Model == "Quadratic", predict(model_quadratic), predict(model_cubic))
)

# Plot the best time trend
ggplot(data, aes(x = time, y = GCC)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, color = "gray") +
  geom_line(aes(y = fitted), color = "blue", size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = paste("Best Time Trend for GCC Thickness:", best_model$Model),
    x = "Time (years)",
    y = "Predicted GCC Thickness (microns)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
# Load the necessary library
library(nlme)
library(dplyr)

# Transform `time` into consecutive integers for each individual
data <- data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(time_int = rank(time)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Fit models with different covariance structures
models <- list()

# 1. Random Intercept Only (RI)
models$RI <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, data = data, method = "REML")

# 2. Random Intercept and Slope (RIAS)
models$RIAS <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ time | id, data = data, method = "REML")

# 3. Compound Symmetry (CS)
models$CS <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corCompSymm(form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# 4. Autoregressive of order 1 (AR(1))
models$AR1 <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corAR1(form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# 5. Autoregressive Moving Average (ARMA(1,1))
models$ARMA11 <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corARMA(p = 1, q = 1, form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# 6. ARMA(2,1)
models$ARMA21 <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corARMA(p = 2, q = 1, form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# 7. ARMA(2,0)
models$ARMA20 <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, correlation = corARMA(p = 2, q = 0, form = ~ time | id), data = data, method = "REML")

# 8. Toeplitz covariance structure (TOEP)
models$TOEP <- lme(
  fixed = GCC ~ time,
  random = ~ 1 | id,
  correlation = corAR1(form = ~ time | id),  # AR(1) for a Toeplitz-like structure
  data = data,
  method = "REML"
)

# Compare models using AIC
model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = names(models),
  AIC = sapply(models, AIC)
)

# Sort models by AIC (lower is better)
model_comparison <- model_comparison[order(model_comparison$AIC), ]

# Print the comparison table
print(model_comparison)

```

)
model_comparison <- model_comparison[order(model_comparison$AIC), ]

```{r}
# Fit a Random Intercept and Slope (RIAS) model
model_rias <- lme(fixed = GCC ~ time, random = ~time | id, data = data, method = "REML")

# Extract the fixed-effect slope (population average rate of GCC loss)
population_rate <- summary(model_rias)$tTable["time", "Value"]

# Extract random effects (individual slopes)
random_effects <- ranef(model_rias)

# Extract individual slopes (random slopes added to the fixed slope)
individual_rates <- random_effects$time + population_rate

# Summarize individual rates
individual_rate_summary <- data.frame(
  Mean = mean(individual_rates),
  SD = sd(individual_rates),
  Min = min(individual_rates),
  Max = max(individual_rates)
)

# Print the results
cat("Population rate of GCC loss:", round(population_rate, 3), "microns/year\n")
cat("Summary of individual rates:\n")
print(individual_rate_summary)

```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Calculate population average rate of GCC loss using linear regression
population_model <- lm(GCC ~ time, data = data)

# Extract the fixed effect for time (slope)
population_rate_of_change <- coef(population_model)["time"]

# Estimate individual slopes using linear regression for each patient
data_individual_slopes <- data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarize(
    individual_slope = coef(lm(GCC ~ time))["time"], # Slope for each individual
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Summarize individual slopes
slope_summary <- data_individual_slopes %>%
  summarize(
    min_slope = min(individual_slope),
    max_slope = max(individual_slope),
    mean_slope = mean(individual_slope),
    sd_slope = sd(individual_slope)
  )

# Print results
cat("Population Average Rate of GCC Loss:\n")
cat(sprintf(" %.3f microns per year\n", population_rate_of_change))

cat("\nIndividual Variability in Rate of GCC Loss:\n")
cat(sprintf(" Range: %.3f to %.3f microns per year\n", slope_summary$min_slope, slope_summary$max_slope))
cat(sprintf(" Mean: %.3f microns per year\n", slope_summary$mean_slope))
cat(sprintf(" SD: %.3f microns per year\n", slope_summary$sd_slope))

# Plot distribution of individual slopes
ggplot(data_individual_slopes, aes(x = individual_slope)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 3: Distribution of Individual Rates of GCC Loss",
    x = "Rate of GCC Loss (microns/year)",
    y = "Frequency"
  )

```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(nlme)
library(ggplot2)

# Base Model: Population intercept and slope only
base_model <- lme(
  fixed = GCC ~ time, 
  random = ~ time | id,  # Random intercept and slope
  data = data,
  method = "REML"
)

# Include Age: Age-adjusted model
age_model <- lme(
  fixed = GCC ~ time + base_age,  # Add base_age as a fixed effect
  random = ~ time | id,           # Random intercept and slope
  data = data,
  method = "REML"
)

# Summarize and compare models
base_summary <- summary(base_model)
age_summary <- summary(age_model)

# Print model summaries
cat("Base Model (No Age):\n")
print(base_summary)

cat("\nAge-Adjusted Model:\n")
print(age_summary)

# Extract fixed effects for interpretation
fixed_effects_age <- fixef(age_model)
cat("\nFixed Effects in Age-Adjusted Model:\n")
print(fixed_effects_age)

# Visualize the effects of age on GCC trends
ggplot(data, aes(x = time, y = GCC, group = id, color = base_age)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7, size = 0.6) +  # Use lines for better differentiation by age
  scale_color_gradient(low = "blue", high = "red") +  # Gradient color for age
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 6: Effect of Age on GCC Trends",
    x = "Time (years)",
    y = "GCC Thickness (microns)",
    color = "Base Age"
  )

```
